title: Help Needed - Please and Thank you!
author: Preparation_Few
selftext:
Hey everyone!

My partner and I are a two-person indie team, and we've spent the last several months developing our first Steam game, **Lawncrest Mall**.

It's an anomaly horror game set inside an abandoned 1990s shopping mall, and we recently released our free demo.

We're at the point where we could really use some fresh eyes on it. We're especially interested in what people enjoy, what feels confusing or frustrating, and what might make someone stop playing.

We're not looking for compliments or wishlists. We genuinely want to make the game better, and sometimes that means hearing the stuff that isn't working. 😂

If anyone has a little time to give it a try, we'd really appreciate your honest thoughts!

**Free Steam Demo:**  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5348220/Lawncrest\_Mall/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5348220/Lawncrest_Mall/)

Thanks for taking a look!

Matthew & Peter  
Halfway Home Games

comments.author: Ok-Skin-3699
comments.body:
Exit: Mall then? It seems neat, though I have my reservations about how much of that game's success was it's "spot the difference" format over its creativity and humour.

What stops the loops from feeling tedious? Is there lore to encounter or stuff to find while I try and remember what these rooms look like? Or could I have just bought ISpy books and a shock collar for the same experience?

The monster idea is neat, but the gifs of it on the steam page make it look so non threatening I mentally dismissed it till I remembered just now it existed.

replies.author: Preparation_Few
replies.body: I appreciate the feedback but Exit 8 wasn't the first anomaly game and this one won't be last. The point is to spot the differences in creepy conditions and keeping in mind that this is a demo and only a sample of what is to come. One thing I would say ... You basically just judged a book by it's cover. You offered feedback and then basically said you only offered it from the pictures.

replies.author: Ok-Skin-3699
replies.body:
You're right, but that's how most people are gonna scan your steam page, I'd argue most people that land on the page wont even click the read more button to read the description. I totally respect its not the kind of feedback you were looking for, but it did impact my decision to engage with your game, in that I didn't download the demo.

I wish yall the best though! I dont remember other high profile games in this genre other than the scp inspired security cam one whose name i forget.
